name: Example: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Using the Sum and Product Rules
worked_solution:
Since the domain of integration $R = [1,2] \times \left[0,\pi/2\right] \times [1,4]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{dx}{x}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy{\int }_{1}^{4}dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,dx{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,{\int }_{1}^{4}dz & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|]_{1}^{2}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2}\cdot (4-1) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))\cdot 3 \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0)\cdot (0+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\int_{1}^{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{1}^{4} \dfrac{\sin{y}}{x} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x = 3\ln 2.
$$
